title: evals/ directory missing tsconfig.json causes root npm run build to fail

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable bug report identifying that the evals/ directory contains TypeScript files but lacks a tsconfig.json, causing root-level build and typecheck commands to fail.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Adding evals/tsconfig.json and ensuring it extends the root TypeScript configuration and properly maps module path references is a localized configuration update.

summary.problem: The evals/ directory contains TypeScript files but lacks a tsconfig.json configuration, causing root-level build and typecheck processes to fail.
summary.root_cause: The root build/typecheck command (tsc -b) or package build processes expect all subdirectories containing TypeScript files, such as evals/, to have a valid tsconfig.json extending the root tsconfig.json and referencing project dependencies like @google/gemini-cli-core and @google/gemini-cli.
summary.context: Other subdirectories like integration-tests/, memory-tests/, and perf-tests/ have dedicated tsconfig.json files that extend ../tsconfig.json and define path mappings or project references.

steps: Create or update evals/tsconfig.json extending ../tsconfig.json with noEmit: true, path mappings for @google/gemini-cli-core and @google/gemini-cli, and project references to ../packages/core and ../packages/cli.
Update package.json to include evals/tsconfig.json in the root typecheck script (tsc -b evals/tsconfig.json ...).

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Running npm run typecheck or npm run build at the repository root completes successfully without TypeScript configuration errors for the evals/ directory.
verification_steps: Run npm run typecheck at root to verify tsc -b evals/tsconfig.json passes without errors.
Run npm run build at root to ensure full build execution succeeds.
